title: Bessie Coleman's birth chart
metaDescription: Bessie Coleman's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 6.3° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Neptune sit 0.1° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads identity and imagination as a single working part. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aquarius, but precisely: 6.3°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (13.0°), Venus in Pisces (7.6°), Mars in Sagittarius (1.2°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste tuned to mood and undertow, drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun trine Neptune, 0.1° of separation. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, the Sun square Uranus at 0.3°, and Neptune conjunction Pluto at 0.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: the Sun, Saturn, Neptune close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it. Mars opposes Neptune while both square Venus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aquarius at 6.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 7.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Pisces at 18.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives air 3, water 3, earth 2, fire 1, and mutable 6, fixed 2, cardinal 1 across the modes. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.2° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
